subject: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Miller <jessica.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@finapp.io>, procure@acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options

Hi Jessica,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Per our call, I wanted to summarize a compact set of options for Acme's support and SLA coverage so your procurement and engineering teams can pick what best matches your risk profile and budget. Attached is a quick grid (SLA_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx) and a draft mutual action plan (Acme_MA_plan_draft.docx).

Key options:
- Bronze: 99.5% uptime, business-hours email triage, 24-hour response for Sev 1 with escalation to engineering lead. No retainer; per-incident credits.
- Silver: 99.9% uptime, 4-hour response for Sev 1, 24/7 on-call for escalation during major incidents, 1 FTE-equivalent retainer credit included. 5% volume discount at 12-month commit.
- Gold (recommended): 99.95% uptime SLA, 1-hour response for Sev 1, 24/7 named on-call rotation, runbooks and quarterly DR drills, 10% volume discount at 12-month commit + optional named CSM.

We can also blend: keep Gold response SLAs with a lower retainer and alternate a consumption-based uplift. As a gesture for being an early platform partner, we can offer a fee credit equal to one month of committed spend if you sign a 12-month committed plan.

Questions for you so we can prepare a formal quote:
1) Which uptime band would you want enforceable in contract (Bronze/Silver/Gold)?
2) Do you need named on-call (Gold) or is an escalations roster sufficient?
3) Any procurement constraints around volume commit vs. monthly true-up?

I looped in Tom and procurement in case there are PO or billing constraints. If helpful, I can provide a short two-page amendment that maps these options to contract language.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: SLA_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Acme_MA_plan_draft.docx (doc)

From: Jessica Miller <jessica.miller@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options

Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear options and the spreadsheet. Quick responses below:
- Prefer Silver minimum, but given our compliance requirements we want the option to scale to Gold for critical apps.
- Named on-call is expensive for our finance team; would accept an escalation roster + guaranteed 4-hour SLAT for Sev 1 during business hours, and 2-hour for Sev 1 if we opt into Gold.
- Procurement: we have to avoid fixed annual prepayments unless offset by firm credits — monthly true-up is preferred. However, we can consider a 9–12 month commit if there is a sensible credit structure and an early-termination clause.

Two asks before we can present to procurement:
1) Can you quantify the retainer credit and the early-adopter one-month credit (line items) so I can show a net-first-year cost?
2) Any flexibility on the cost delta between Silver and Gold for the first 6 months?

Tom and procurement are copied. If you can send a single-page commercial summary and a redlineable term sheet that maps the options to specific language, that would speed review.

Best,
Jessica
Head of SRE | Acme Corp
jessica.miller@acme.com

On Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options — Acme follow-up

Team — forwarding Acme's reply. They lean Silver as a baseline but will consider Gold with credits. Procurement is sensitive to prepay. They asked for:
- line-item retainer credit and early-adopter one-month credit broken out
- a short commercial summary + redlineable term sheet mapping the options to language

My proposed commercial posture:
- Keep monthly true-up to accommodate their procurement constraints. Offer a 12-month commit with the following trade: 7% volume discount + a first-month spend credit (equal to monthly committed amount) if they sign within 30 days.
- For Gold response SLA (1-hour) make the named on-call optional at an additional fixed monthly fee. This reduces near-term headcount risk.
- If they opt to scale from Silver->Gold mid-term, pro-rate the retainer monthly with a 30-day notice; escalation rotation takes effect after 14-day onboarding window.

Grace — can you run an estimate for Gold per-MAU impact and the possible nominal fee for named on-call? Keep the estimate conservative; I want margin to move in negotiation. Also, please flag any operational constraints for providing the 1-hour response SLA for the first 90 days post-onboarding.

Aditya — will need a short commercial brief (single page) and a draft terms amendment we can send to Acme. I can handle the negotiation and procurement calls.

Thanks,
Vanessa

--- Forwarded attachment: SLA_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jessica Miller <jessica.miller@acme.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@finapp.io>, procure@acme.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options

Hi all,

Thanks for the clear ask, Vanessa and Jessica. Per the operational review:
- We can support the Silver package (99.9% + 4-hour Sev1) with existing on-call roster with no additional headcount.
- For Gold (99.95% + 1-hour Sev1 + named on-call) we recommend the "named on-call" be provided as a paid add-on at $8,500/month to cover guaranteed rotation slots and escalation preparedness; that fee also funds quarterly DR drills and runbook alignment.
- Retainer credit: We can apply a credit equal to one week of committed monthly spend for every quarter of committed contract (i.e., 1 week credit per quarter, capped at 4 weeks total) OR a one-month credit for an immediate 12-month commit signed within 30 days. Either is contract-friendly.
- Early months: to reduce risk in the onboarding window, for the first 60 days we will offer a response-promise of 2 hours for Sev1 on Gold (not contractually binding SLA) while we complete DR playbook integration; after that period 1-hour SLA begins.

Commercial summary (high level):
- Silver: list price $X/mo, baseline 4-hour Sev1, no named on-call. 5% discount at 12 months (monthly true-up).
- Gold: list price $Y/mo, 1-hour Sev1, named on-call add-on $8.5k/mo, 10% discount at 12 months (monthly true-up).
- Signing incentive: one-month spend credit for 12-month commit signed within 30 days, or quarterly retainer credits as above.

Attached is a one-page commercial brief and a redline-friendly term amendment (link: https://docs.redwood.com/contract-templates/acme-mau-term-sheet). Vanessa — if you want, I can draft a short email that maps each commercial line to contract language for procurement.

Jessica / Tom — happy to hop on a call to walk procurement through the math.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachments: commercial_summary_onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Miller <jessica.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@finapp.io>, procure@acme.com, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pricing flexibility and escalation coverage options

Jessica — thanks for the clarity. Attached is the single-page commercial summary and a redline-friendly amendment (link below). Condensed response to your two asks:
1) Credits: the signing incentive equals one month of committed spend (applied as an invoice credit). Example: if committed monthly baseline is $80k, credit = $80k applied in month 2 invoice. Alternatively, choose the quarterly credit schedule (1 week credit per quarter capped at 4 weeks).
2) Cost delta flexibility: we can absorb a 15% discount on Gold pricing for the first 6 months (applied as a rebate on invoices) if you take a 12-month commit with monthly true-up and agree to the early-termination clause (90-day termination with pro-rata repayment of signing credit). After month 6, pricing reverts to negotiated discount band.

Next steps:
- If that posture is acceptable, we'll send a redlineable amendment and the commercial brief.
- Schedule a 30-minute procurement walkthrough next week to go over contract language and the onboarding calendar.

Proposed time: Tue 16 Feb, 10:00 AM PST — ok for you and Tom?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
